candidates: When modifying the `build:types` script (currently driven by `.build/types.ts`), ensure TypeScript declaration generation runs in strict package-dependency order — `parser` first, then `mermaid`, then remaining packages — because each downstream package's compilation depends on the previous stage's emitted `.d.ts` files. Parallel strategies such as `pnpm --recursive exec tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` break this ordering and will produce type errors.

When creating a new package in this monorepo, audit its `devDependencies` and `scripts` for any `standard`-related entries (the linting tool the project previously used) and remove them; the project has migrated to `prettier` for formatting, so `standard` deps and scripts are no longer needed.

In external diagram/plugin packages (e.g. `mermaid-flowchart-elk`, `mermaid-zenuml`), declare `mermaid` as a `peerDependency` — not a `devDependency` — using the `workspace:^` protocol (e.g. `"mermaid": "workspace:^"`). This ensures `pnpm publish` automatically resolves to the correct released version and prevents breaking downstream consumers when mermaid introduces breaking changes.
